lead.headline: The chestnut festival brings the biggest market in a decade

photo.caption: The autumn market stalls being set up on Thursday in the Plaza Mayor. Photo: Town Hall archive.

lead.body:
More than fifty stalls will fill the Plaza Mayor and the nearby streets on November 1, in the biggest chestnut festival market anyone can remember. Forty producers from the area, among them eleven bakeries, seven cheesemakers and three honey cooperatives, will sell directly to the public.

The organizers expect some five thousand people to visit the market over the day, twice as many as five years ago. “We have had to borrow the high school parking lot,” jokes Anna Bosch, president of the shopkeepers' association.

Besides the stalls, there will be live music from eleven in the morning, a chestnut bread workshop for children run by the Cal Forn bakery, and a **big public chestnut roast** in the square at five in the afternoon.

The Town Hall will close the village center to traffic from seven in the morning to nine at night. Residents will be able to reach their garages via Calle del Molí, through a checkpoint staffed by the Local Police.

Anyone who would like to volunteer can sign up at the tourist office until October 28. Hands are needed for setting up, information and waste collection, and those who take part will be invited to the organizers' lunch.
lead.quote: “We have watched everything sold here grow, from cheese to honey.”

feature.headline: Three trails to enjoy the beech forest

photo.alt: A path between meadows with mountains in the background
photo.caption: The Pla de les Eres trail on an October Sunday. Photo: Joan Casas.

feature.body:
October is beech forest month. Here are three outings to enjoy it without the crowds, from the shortest to the most demanding:

- **The Molí path** (1 h 30 min, 4 km, suitable for children): starts at the factory parking lot and follows the river up to a small waterfall.
- **The Pla de les Eres loop** (3 h, 9 km): meadows, farmhouses and a viewpoint over the whole area.
- **The Sant Roc ridge** (5 h, 14 km): only in good weather and with hiking boots; ++best to set off before eight++.

Remember to carry water, stay on the marked trails and take back with you any waste you produce.

briefs:
## New library opening hours

Starting in November, the municipal library will also open on Saturday mornings, from ten to one. The change is possible thanks to two new staff positions and a group of volunteers who are already preparing the children's activities.

## Roadworks on the Olot road

The improvement works on the road will begin on November 10 and last about six weeks. Traffic will be controlled with temporary lights, and a shuttle bus will run between the two villages at peak hours.

## The book club turns ten

It will celebrate with a dinner on November 22 at the community center. Anyone who wants to come must sign up a week in advance and bring a book for the exchange.

## Clothing drive

Cáritas is collecting warm clothing from November 3 to 14. The drop-off points are the parish church, the community center and the sports center.
